### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. hawkinsinuria  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.414)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-8963684)

**Proposed mechanism:** HGD (Heme oxygenase 1) (HGNC:4892) —DISRUPTS→ Homogentisic acid (CHEBI:17183); Homogentisic acid (CHEBI:17183) —DISRUPTS→ Tyrosine catabolism (R-HSA-8963684); Tyrosine catabolism (R-HSA-8963684) —LEADS_TO→ Dark urine (HP:0001877); Tyrosine catabolism (R-HSA-8963684) —LEADS_TO→ Ochronosis (HP:0001042); HPD (4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate dioxygenase) (HGNC:4891) —DISRUPTS→ 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate (CHEBI:17703); 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate (CHEBI:17703) —DISRUPTS→ Tyrosine catabolism (R-HSA-8963684). Loss-of-function mutations in HGD (Alkaptonuria) or HPD (Hawkinsinuria) disrupt the tyrosine catabolism pathway, leading to the accumulation of homogentisic acid and 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate, respectively. These metabolites aberrantly enter downstream pathways, contributing to the characteristic phenotypes of dark urine and ochronosis.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in HGD or HPD do not lead to loss-of-function or that the accumulation of homogentisic acid or 4-hydroxyphenylpyruvate does not occur in affected individuals. _(variant: Absence of pathogenic loss-of-function variants in HGD and HPD in relevant control populations (e.g., gnomAD).)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared pathway disruption in tyrosine catabolism offers potential for developing common therapeutic strategies targeting metabolite accumulation or downstream effects for both Alkaptonuria and Hawkinsinuria.

#### 2. tyrosinemia type III  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.404)
